parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs a national layer of genuine universal-exposure measures — passport/visa sex-marker scrutiny with a documented refusals-and-fraud pathway, entry screening that can out travellers, and national facility/custody rules — against a state layer with no current facility ban (the 2016 law was repealed), no presentation offence, and partial municipal protections. The visitor's sharpest exposures are at entry/documents and, if a minor travels along, closed minor care and school-notification rules; state custody bars transition care. Recourse is thin: the state hate-crime statute excludes gender identity and there is no statewide accommodation protection. That places this above unremedied-ban jurisdictions but below jurisdictions with working protections and documented acceptance.

entry_documents.exposure: Documented: national cable directs refusal where sex is doubted; wilful misrepresentation may trigger lifetime fraud ineligibility; X-marker processing stopped; travellers reported passports confiscated/blocked and stranding; allied governments issued advisories after detentions.
entry_documents.protection: Fraud finding requires four elements, is never automatic, waivers exist; litigation ongoing; legal-aid FAQ exists.
entry_documents.interaction: Document doubt at entry can escalate to refusal or fraud investigation before any state-level rule applies.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented nationally: corrections bureau policies removing hormones and enforcing forced presentation; immigration-custody forced labour, beatings, sexual abuse of trans men. State custody bars public transition care.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any visa/entry dispute can route a visitor into national custody with these documented practices.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National funding-based facility restrictions; national executive order bars trans use of congruent single-sex facilities in funded settings. State currently has NO facility ban — 2016 law repealed 2017; no criminalisation of facility use; 2025 bill pending but text/status unestablished.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State repeal is operative; largest city and one county ordinances cover gender identity (~30% of population).
federal_state_facilities.interaction: National-funded facilities still restrict; state position could change within a legislative term.

care_services.exposure: Minor care fully banned (2023 veto overrides, effective for any accompanying trans minor); state funds barred for transition care in custody; national funding freeze and proposed insurance rules; 2025 law keeps original marker displayed on amended certificates.
care_services.protection: Adult visitors can ordinarily obtain care; hospital visitation statute exists.
care_services.interaction: A travelling minor loses access to continued blockers/HRT; custody placement compounds it.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Documented: executive orders framing trans minors' care as 'mutilation'; counterterrorism strategy targeting 'radically pro-transgender' groups; criminal-prosecution directive for teachers facilitating transition; 'forbidden terms' purges.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Several orders blocked or enjoined; courts remain contested; hate-crime statute covers gender identity nationally.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat-framing raises outing severity and legitimates official suspicion at entry and schools.

minors_guardians.exposure: Documented: minor care banned; teacher-prosecution order; school parent-notification laws; national subpoena of hospital records of under-19s; athletics ban applies to visiting trans athletes.
minors_guardians.protection: None documented at state level for visiting minors.
minors_guardians.interaction: Guardian risks investigation exposure if the minor socially transitions or seeks care.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: State hate-crime statute excludes gender identity and sexual orientation — bias assault may not be charged as bias crime; 2022 killing-rate figure is an acknowledged undercount without denominator; no statewide accommodation protection.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Municipal ordinances in largest city/county; national hate-crime statute; documented 2020 arrest under another state's law is out-of-state.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police charging options narrow if a visitor is assaulted outside ordinance-covered cities.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Statewide private accommodation/employment protection absent; county application of amended-certificate rules unclear; 2025 bathroom bill status unknown; enforcement practice at facilities unknown.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Litigation ongoing nationally; local ordinances provide partial recourse.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Open questions weigh lightly; they do not offset documented national exposures.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.35-A has an unremedied universal birth-sex facility rule with confirmed exclusions. Here the state ban was repealed and no statute bars facility use; the operative universal exposures are at documents/entry, so this jurisdiction sits above 0.35-A.

Like 0.55-B, documented hostility and patchy local remedies coexist with genuine welcoming pockets and some functioning recourse (municipal ordinances, national hate-crime law). But the national document/refusal regime here is a stronger universal exposure than ferry-operator hostility, holding the score at the same level, not higher.

0.75-C has a dead-letter statute plus documented acceptance and a working remedy. Here the negative is live, not dead-letter: documented refusals, fraud pathways, minor-care bans and custody harm, so this rates clearly below 0.75-C.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller's operative exposure concentrates at the national border and document layer: a documented pipeline from document doubt to refusal, fraud investigation, and detention where national custody practices are documented as abusive. Once past entry, this state is materially safer than its parent average — no current facility ban, no presentation offence, partial municipal protections — but the state adds its own exposures: closed minor care (severe for a travelling family), a hate-crime statute excluding gender identity, no statewide accommodation protection, barred custody care, and a live legislative movement to reinstate bans. Threat-framing at national level raises the stakes of any outing. Remedies are partial and uneven, so the case sits in elevated risk: above unremedied-ban jurisdictions, below those with documented working protections and acceptance.
